title: Bound a native common-source fan expansion: no paid-moment gain in the declared scope
body:
A common-source fan identity can add a canceling ADD pair while merging two paid Gaussian transitions. This package checks that changed scalar contact graph on the frozen round-three native word instead of assuming that fewer scalar operations improve the recursive moment.

The exact bounded census finds 127,218 admissible forward occurrences and 2,804 backward occurrences under its existing-chart policy and next-80-event horizon. All bills are unchanged except four forward occurrences with delta `2 H1-H2`, which loses for every `0<C<1`. A three-arbitrary-input fixture has the favorable delta `H4-2 H2`, so the mechanism can help in a different contact geometry. The complete integer tariff classification, local proof, one whole-word transport reconstruction per tariff class and exact interval corroboration are included.

No new K, changed admitted native word, phase certificate, or compiler/outer result is claimed. The result fixes the source interfaces, native maps, center jobs, event barriers, contact-frame policy and horizon. Other circuits, contact charts, interacting rewrites and native maps remain outside scope. This route stops here; no larger unchanged-family scan is proposed.

Validation: registered Python 3.12 and optimized direct replays; source pins; committed-byte preflight; official 10-file export and integrity check; optimized export replay with networking disabled and Git absent from PATH; dirty-input identity, profitable frame fixture and wrong-sign control. Full source-history preflight remains unavailable in this shallow checkout. No full historical suite or selected cold replay was run.

Canonical investigation: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5032. Proof, exact counts, scope and open next question are in `research/complex-fan-expansion/`.
